flowPrompt.prompt:
A scroll-stopping 8-second vertical (9:16) space cinematic short, filmed as one smooth continuous take. Gas spiraling into a black hole forms a blazing accretion disk heated to millions of degrees, glowing brightly in X-rays.

SCENE: Deep space with faint background stars.
SUBJECT: A black hole's accretion disk: a flat, spinning whirlpool of superheated gas, deep red at the edge and blinding blue-white near the center.

ACTION:
0–2s: A white-hot whirlpool of gas spins around a black void, its inner edge blazing brighter than its outer rim.
2–6s: The camera descends slowly toward the disk plane as the gas spins faster and glows hotter toward the center, its streaks shifting from red to orange to blue-white.
6–8s: The camera skims level with the disk, showing the brilliant inner edge encircling the black shadow. The final frame holds steady.
Movement: Camera and celestial motion are slow, smooth and majestic. Orbits, gas flows and particles follow believable physics.

Effects: turbulent spiraling gas streaks with one side brightened by its motion.

SOUND: Off-screen voice-over by a calm, deep Indian male documentary narrator with a subtle cinematic reverb, speaking Hindi in an awe-struck, calm and mysterious tone: at 1.2s "गिरती गैस बनाती है accretion disk…", then at 4.2s "लाखों डिग्री गर्म, X-rays में चमकती!". Mix: the Hindi voice stays clear and upfront; the music sits softly underneath and rises in the gaps between lines. Sound effects: roaring whirlpool rush (0.4s), rising electric crackle (3.0s), deep blooming boom (6.0s). Ambience: dense, rumbling energy hum.

KEEP CONSISTENT: Celestial bodies keep the same size, color, texture and relative positions throughout. Background stars stay fixed and steady, with no twinkling flicker. The sense of scale stays vast and consistent. Clean frame without captions, subtitles or logos.

0–2s: A tumbling grey asteroid suddenly lengthens as its near end is dragged toward a pitch-black sphere.

Sound effects: deep groaning rock creak (0.5s), stretching, rising tonal sweep (3.0s), muffled cracking rumble (6.0s). Ambience: low ominous gravitational hum.

flowPrompt.prompt:
A scroll-stopping 8-second vertical (9:16) space cinematic short, filmed as one smooth continuous take. Ganymede, Jupiter's largest moon and the biggest moon in the solar system, glides past the planet Mercury in a side-by-side size comparison.

SCENE: An artistic side-by-side arrangement in space with Jupiter's banded globe in the background.
SUBJECT: Jupiter's moon Ganymede, with patches of dark ancient terrain and bright grooved ice, shown next to the planet Mercury for size comparison.

ACTION:
0–2s: A huge icy moon with dark and bright grooved terrain drifts beside a smaller grey, cratered planet.
2–6s: The camera tracks slowly past Mercury and on to Ganymede, which is visibly larger, its bright grooves catching the sunlight.
6–8s: Both bodies hang side by side, Ganymede clearly the bigger of the two, with Jupiter looming behind. The final frame holds steady.
Movement: Camera and celestial motion are slow, smooth and majestic. Orbits, gas flows and particles follow believable physics.

CAMERA: Side tracking view; smooth lateral dolly; 50 mm lens; smooth and stabilized.
LOOK: Cinematic deep-space realism. Giant-screen space cinematography, deep blacks, luminous nebula colors, gentle lens bloom and an awe-inspiring scale reveal. Lighting: hard sunlight from one side. Color grade: icy grey-brown, cool white and warm Jupiter bands. Effects: a clean size comparison with no labels.

SOUND: Off-screen voice-over by a calm, deep Indian male documentary narrator with a subtle cinematic reverb, speaking Hindi in an awe-struck, calm and mysterious tone: at 1.3s "Solar System का सबसे बड़ा चाँद…", then at 4.5s "Ganymede, Mercury planet से भी बड़ा!". Music: original instrumental, bold, curious orchestral score with plucked strings and rising horns; awe-filled and cinematic, with wide shimmering space and a deep, warm low end, no vocals. A deep cinematic swell starts on the first frame, rises with the camera move, blooms into a huge awe-filled lift at the 6-second reveal, and settles into a soft shimmering fade-out by 8 seconds. Mix: the Hindi voice stays clear and upfront; the music sits softly underneath and rises in the gaps between lines. Sound effects: deep icy rumble (0.5s), smooth passing whoosh (3.0s), bright surprised chord (6.0s). Ambience: low planetary hum.

KEEP CONSISTENT: Celestial bodies keep the same size, color, texture and relative positions throughout. Background stars stay fixed and steady, with no twinkling flicker. The sense of scale stays vast and consistent. Clean frame without captions, subtitles or logos.
notes: Flow settings: choose Veo 3.1, aspect ratio Portrait (9:16). Each clip is 8 seconds.
Best quality: use Frames to Video with the image you made from the Image Prompt as the first frame.
Hindi voice: if the pronunciation isn't clear, generate again, or record the line yourself and add it in YouTube.
If Flow says “might violate our policies”: wait 5–10 minutes and try the same prompt once more (busy servers fail too). If it fails again, report the video number.

Music silent or weak? Use a copyright-free backup: YouTube Studio → Audio Library, filter Genre “Cinematic”, Mood “Bright” and “Attribution not required”. Download a track and add it under the clip in your editor before uploading. Never use a commercial song.

flowPrompt.prompt:
A scroll-stopping 8-second vertical (9:16) space cinematic short, filmed as one smooth continuous take. Radio dishes across the globe link up as one Earth-sized telescope, and their combined view produced the first image of a black hole's shadow, in galaxy Messier 87, released in April 2019.

SCENE: A high-altitude desert observatory at night, rising to a view of the whole Earth and the deep sky beyond.
SUBJECT: A network of radio telescopes across Earth linked by glowing lines, and the resulting blurry orange ring around a dark shadow at the heart of galaxy Messier 87.

ACTION:
0–2s: A huge white radio dish on a high desert plateau tilts toward the night sky under steady stars.
2–6s: The camera rises from the dish into space, revealing points of light on several continents that link up with thin glowing lines across the globe, while a fuzzy orange ring with a dark center slowly forms in the black sky ahead.
6–8s: The glowing orange ring around its dark shadow hangs in the darkness beyond the linked-up Earth. The final frame holds steady.
Movement: Camera and celestial motion are slow, smooth and majestic. Orbits, gas flows and particles follow believable physics.

CAMERA: Low angle beside the dish, rising to orbit; continuous drone rise into a wide space pull-back; 24 mm lens; smooth and stabilized.
LOOK: Cinematic deep-space realism. Giant-screen space cinematography, deep blacks, luminous nebula colors, gentle lens bloom and an awe-inspiring scale reveal. Lighting: moonlit desert, glowing network lines and a warm orange ring glow. Color grade: night blue, white and molten orange. Effects: illustrative glowing network lines between observatories and a soft blurry ring resembling the published image.

SOUND: Off-screen voice-over by a calm, deep Indian male documentary narrator with a subtle cinematic reverb, speaking Hindi in an awe-struck, calm and mysterious tone: at 1.2s "दुनिया भर के telescopes एक साथ जुड़े…", then at 4.2s "2019: black hole की छाया की पहली तस्वीर!". Music: original instrumental, triumphant, soaring orchestral finale with full brass, strings and timpani; awe-filled and cinematic, with wide shimmering space and a deep, warm low end, no vocals. A deep cinematic swell starts on the first frame, rises with the camera move, blooms into a huge awe-filled lift at the 6-second reveal, and settles into a soft shimmering fade-out by 8 seconds. Mix: the Hindi voice stays clear and upfront; the music sits softly underneath and rises in the gaps between lines. Sound effects: mechanical hum of the dish turning (0.5s), electric linking pulses (3.4s), deep triumphant boom (6.2s). Ambience: high desert night wind fading into a space hum.

KEEP CONSISTENT: Celestial bodies keep the same size, color, texture and relative positions throughout. Background stars stay fixed and steady, with no twinkling flicker. The sense of scale stays vast and consistent. Clean frame without captions, subtitles or logos.
notes: Flow settings: choose Veo 3.1, aspect ratio Portrait (9:16). Each clip is 8 seconds.
Best quality: use Frames to Video with the image you made from the Image Prompt as the first frame.
Hindi voice: if the pronunciation isn't clear, generate again, or record the line yourself and add it in YouTube.
If Flow says “might violate our policies”: wait 5–10 minutes and try the same prompt once more (busy servers fail too). If it fails again, report the video number.

Music silent or weak? Use a copyright-free backup: YouTube Studio → Audio Library, filter Genre “Cinematic”, Mood “Inspirational” and “Attribution not required”. Download a track and add it under the clip in your editor before uploading. Never use a commercial song.
